info.title: ISBNdb API Documentation v2
info.description:
Welcome to the ISBNdb API documentation. Our REST API allows you to retrieve
information about millions of books.

## Authentication

Include your API key in the HTTP headers of every request:

```http
GET /book/9780134093413 HTTP/1.1
Host: api2.isbndb.com
Authorization: YOUR_REST_KEY
Accept: */*
```

The header is the only way to authenticate. Passing your API key as a query
parameter is **not** supported — query strings are recorded in server logs,
proxies and browser history, so a key sent that way is far easier to leak. Such a
request is rejected as unauthenticated:

```text
https://api2.isbndb.com/book/9780134093413?Authorization=YOUR_REST_KEY
```

## Error responses

Every error carries the same body, with the reason repeated under two keys.
`errorMessage` is the current one; `message` is kept for older clients. Error
bodies are the one place the API does not use snake_case:

```json
{"message": "Book not found", "errorMessage": "Book not found"}
```

**400 Bad Request** — the request is invalid or fails validation, for example
an incorrect ISBN format, a query over 150 characters, or a filter combination
the endpoint does not allow.

**401 Unauthorized** — your API key is missing, unknown, or the subscription
behind it is inactive. The reason differs by case: `Full authentication is
required to access this resource.` when no key was sent, `Bad credentials.`
when the key is unknown, `Api key is not active` when the subscription lapsed.

**404 Not Found** — the requested ISBN is not in our database:

```json
{"message": "Book not found", "errorMessage": "Book not found"}
```

**429 Too Many Requests** — the per minute or the daily limit of your plan is
reached:

```json
{"message": "Per minute quota exceeded, please try again later"}
```

```json
{"message": "Daily quota exceeded, please try again later"}
```

**503 Service Unavailable** — the search backend is briefly unreachable. Retry
after the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

***Note on 404 errors: a 404 response indicates that the book information is not
yet available in our database. However, due to frequent updates, there is a high
probability that the data will be added shortly, often within a minute or up to
24 hours. We recommend trying your request again after a while, as the
information may soon become accessible.***

## Rate limits

You can programmatically monitor your usage and limits by inspecting the
standard `ratelimit-policy` and `ratelimit` headers we send with every response:

**`ratelimit-policy`** defines the limit rules of your subscription plan, where
`q` is the quota (maximum allowed requests) and `w` is the window (timeframe in
seconds):

```text
ratelimit-policy: "rate";q=300;w=60
ratelimit-policy: "daily";q=50000;w=86400
```

**`ratelimit`** displays your current real-time usage status, where `r` is the
number of requests left in the window and `t` is how many seconds you have to
wait before the next request is allowed. While you still have quota, `t` is `0`
— there is nothing to wait for:

```text
ratelimit: "rate";r=297;t=0
ratelimit: "daily";r=48999;t=56312
```

All daily limits reset at **00:00 UTC** every day.

## Pagination

Paginated endpoints take `page` and `pageSize` as query parameters and echo them
back as `page` and `page_size` in the response body. Query parameters are
camelCase, response fields are snake_case — that difference is intentional and
applies across the whole API (error bodies excepted, see above).

On the search and detail endpoints `pageSize` is capped at **100**: a larger value
is rejected with a **400 Bad Request**. Subscriptions that existed before the cap
was introduced keep the previous limit of 1,000 — where a larger value is quietly
reduced instead of rejected — until **October 10, 2026**, after which the cap of
100 applies to every key. Paging stops at 10,000 results — a request whose offset
would reach past that is answered with a **400 Bad Request**, and the last page
before the ceiling is trimmed to fit. `total` is likewise counted only up to
10,000, so a broad query reports exactly `10000` instead of the real figure.
Narrow the query rather than paging deeper.

`GET /feeds/books/updates` paginates differently: there is no 10,000 ceiling and
no `total`, and a `pageSize` above 1,000 is rejected with a **400 Bad Request**
instead of being reduced. Keep requesting pages until `data` comes back empty.

## Null values

Fields with no value are left out of the response rather than sent as `null`.
The schemas below mark them nullable, but in practice you should treat a missing
key and a null value the same way.

get.description:
Returns the book details. 
        
**A 404 Not Found response for an ISBN lookup typically indicates that the book information is not yet available
in our database. However, due to frequent updates, there is a high probability that the data will be added shortly,
often within a minute or up to 24 hours. We recommend trying your request again after a while, as the information
may soon become accessible.**

parameters.name: isbn
parameters.description: An ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, with or without hyphens. The response always reports the book under its ISBN-13.

parameters.name: with_prices
parameters.description:
Whether to include prices in the response. 

***Requires a plan with price access (Pro and above).*** On plans without it the parameter is ignored and the book is returned without prices - the request is not rejected.

***Performance Impact:*** Enabling this will increase response time, as current prices are fetched from vendors in real-time.

post.description:
Retrieves a list of books matching the provided array of ISBNs. This endpoint is available on all plans and does not use pagination.

**Request Limits per Plan:**
* **Academic:** Up to 10 ISBNs per request.
* **Basic:** Up to 100 ISBNs per request.
* **Pro, Premium, and higher:** Up to 1,000 ISBNs per request.

Exceeding the limit returns a **400 Bad Request** naming the exact limit for your plan.

**Quota Usage (Important):** Each requested ISBN counts as a separate API call against your daily limit. For example, a single request containing 100 ISBNs will deduct 100 calls from your daily quota. Duplicates are collapsed and unusable ISBNs are discarded before the charge is calculated, so the amount actually deducted is the `requested` field of the response.

**Response Behavior:**
* The response will only include books that successfully match an ISBN in our database. 
* Any submitted ISBNs that are not found will be silently ignored and excluded from the response.
* **Note:** Pricing information is not returned by this endpoint.

get.description:
Retrieves a list of book ISBNs that have been added or modified. This endpoint is designed for frequent incremental synchronization.

**Important Notes:**
* **Plan limits:** Available exclusively for **Premium** plans and higher. Other plans get a **403 Forbidden**.
* **History limit:** The update history is strictly limited to the last **7 days**.
* **Quota:** Calling this endpoint does not count towards your daily API limits.
* **Pagination:** The response does not include a total field. To fetch all updates, continue requesting subsequent pages (incrementing the page parameter) until the data array in the response is empty.

get.description:
Field-level search over the book catalogue.

**At least one filter is required.** Supply either an identifier (`isbn` or `isbn13`) or one or more
search fields (`author`, `text`, `subject`, `publisher`). Mixing the two groups is rejected with a
**400 Bad Request**, and so is sending none of them.

Passing `isbn` or `isbn13` skips the search index and resolves the book directly.

This endpoint does not return pricing information.

get.description: Returns the name and a list of books by the subject.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The subject name. **Max length: 150 characters**.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Filter by language. Matches the ISO 639-3 code held in the index, e.g. `eng` for English, `fra` for French. On `/books/{query}` full names and two-letter codes are normalised for you; every other endpoint matches the code exactly.

schema.description: Filter by language. Matches the ISO 639-3 code held in the index, e.g. `eng` for English, `fra` for French. On `/books/{query}` full names and two-letter codes are normalised for you; every other endpoint matches the code exactly.

isbns.description: ISBN-10 or ISBN-13 values to look up. The maximum number of ISBNs per request depends on the plan: 10 on Academic, 100 on Basic, 1,000 on Pro and above. Each ISBN counts as a separate call against the daily quota.

year.description: Filter books by year of publication

shouldMatchAll.description:
If set to `1` or `true`, the API will return books where the title 
        or author exactly contains all the words entered by the user.

column.description:
Search limited to this column:
* `` - Empty value search in every column
* `title` - Only searches in Books Title
* `author` - Only searches books by the given Author
* `date_published` - Only searches books in a given year, e.g. 1998
* `subjects` - Only searches books by the given subject, e.g. physics

pages.description: Number of pages in the book

dimensions.description: Physical dimensions of the book as a formatted string
dimensions.example: Height: 11.1 Inches, Length: 9 Inches, Weight: 7.6 Pounds, Width: 1.8 Inches

overview.description: Never populated. Present in the schema for backwards compatibility only; use `synopsis`.

image.description: Cover image link, always present. Maximum height is 500px; the image itself may be a placeholder if no cover is on file.

excerpt.description: Short excerpt from the book. Rarely available.

synopsis.description: Full synopsis or summary of the book

authors.description: List of authors of the book

subjects.description: List of subjects or categories the book belongs to

reviews.description: Never populated. Present in the schema for backwards compatibility only.

related.description: Never populated. Present in the schema for backwards compatibility only; use `other_isbns`.

other_isbns.description: Other ISBNs associated with this book (e.g. different formats or editions)

BadRequest.description: The request failed validation, for example a malformed ISBN, a query longer than 150 characters, or `year` combined with `publishedFrom`/`publishedTo`.

Unauthorized.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or holds an unknown key, or the subscription behind the key is not active. Passing the key as a query parameter is not supported.

TooManyRequests.description: The per minute or the daily quota of the plan is exhausted. The `ratelimit` header states how long until the window resets; daily quotas reset at 00:00 UTC.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service is temporarily unavailable. Retry after the number of seconds given in `Retry-After`.
